title: Make Athena's own writers avoid boundary words in requests and records
summary: The steward, Hestia's error review and root-cause requests, and the introspection writer must run their text through the boundary scan before writing. Any boundary word is replaced with a plain alternative such as 'the person running Athena', so written proposals and requests pass admission and approve-work succeeds. The audience is the person running Athena, who approves proposals, and the admission scan that judges them.

defaults_applied.how: Per-writer tests and an approve-work test; cargo test and clippy -D warnings must pass.
Criteria check the written text against boundary_scan and approve_work succeeding.
One shared check used by every writer, instead of fixing only the steward proposal that failed.
Tests enforce that each writer's output passes the scan.
Behavior criteria name cargo commands the verifier can run.
Doc comments and the changelog entry are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs (boundary_words, boundary_fragments, boundary_scan, which matches whole words case-insensitively plus fragments and returns BoundaryHit line and term), crates/athena-core/src/work_decisions.rs (approve_work builds the request from the work item and goes through normal admission), crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs (ProposedChange::from_change, render, blind_spot_change), crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs (root_cause_request) and crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs. Admission runs check_boundary_and_repo_files in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs.

The fix is one shared sanitiser, built on boundary_scan and boundary_words, that rewrites boundary words to plain alternatives (the person running Athena for the first word in the list, and similar for the others). Each writer calls it before text is written; writers that cannot rewrite safely return an error that names the word.

No new record or data file is added under crates/, so the records allow-list (check_record_file, AnyRecord) is not touched. The shared helper may live in one of the three listed files or in athena-context next to boundary_scan, which is an extra deliverable.

Hestia's error review writer lives in hestia.rs, and the introspection writer in introspect.rs. Fixtures must build the boundary word from fragments so no tracked file contains it, because the repository policy scan fails on tracked files.
This change makes writers refuse or rewrite more text but adds no new admission rule, so no replay refusal-rate criterion is needed: the admission scan itself is unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. A test per writer (steward proposal, Hestia error review, Hestia root-cause request, introspection writer) feeds a fixture whose source text holds a boundary word (built from fragments) and asserts the written text has no hits from boundary_scan and says 'the person running Athena' or another plain alternative.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. A test seeds a steward proposal from a source with a boundary word, calls approve_work, and asserts it succeeds and the submitted request passes check_boundary_and_repo_files.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass, including `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that writers now keep boundary words out of proposals and requests, with no boundary word in the entry itself.
steward.rs, hestia.rs and introspect.rs each call the shared boundary check before writing text that becomes a request or record; a Grep of the diff shows the call in all three.

out_of_scope: Changing the boundary word list or the admission scan's rules
departures: Three writers across three modules plus an approve-work test make this larger than a typical change, so cost and time sit above the reference.
hard_reason: Changes what text Athena's own writers emit into requests and records that the admission scan refuses, and tests the approve-work admission path.
